cls: Topoisomerase I inhibitor; cytotoxic antineoplastic (camptothecin analogue)
pharm: Binds the topoisomerase I-DNA complex, preventing religation of single-strand DNA breaks and causing lethal double-strand breaks during replication

summary: Topotecan is a semisynthetic camptothecin analogue and topoisomerase I inhibitor used as an antineoplastic agent. The intravenous form is indicated for patients with small cell lung cancer (SCLC) with platinum-sensitive disease who progressed at least 60 days after first-line chemotherapy (the IV form is also used for metastatic ovarian carcinoma and, in combination with cisplatin, for cervical carcinoma per its broader labelling). It is given as 1.5 mg/m2 by IV infusion over 30 minutes daily for 5 consecutive days, repeated every 21 days. It carries a BOXED WARNING for severe myelosuppression: the first cycle should only be given to patients with a baseline neutrophil count >=1500/mm3 and platelets >=100,000/mm3, and blood counts must be monitored. Dosing is verified by body surface area and a single IV dose should not exceed 4 mg. The dose is reduced in moderate renal impairment. It can cause fetal harm.
indications: Small cell lung cancer (SCLC) with platinum-sensitive disease that progressed at least 60 days after initiation of first-line chemotherapy (IV)
Metastatic carcinoma of the ovary after failure of initial or subsequent chemotherapy (IV, per broader labelling)
Stage IVB, recurrent, or persistent cervical carcinoma not amenable to curative surgery/radiation, in combination with cisplatin (IV, per broader labelling)

dosage.t: Verify dose using body surface area; do not exceed a single dose of 4 mg
dosage.n: Continue until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity

dosage.d: Reduce to 1.25 mg/m2/day for neutrophils <500/mm3, or administer G-CSF; do not start a subsequent cycle until neutrophils >1000/mm3, platelets >100,000/mm3, haemoglobin >=9 g/dL
dosage.t: Transfuse to support haemoglobin as needed
Insufficient data and not recommended if CLcr <20 mL/min

admin: Cytotoxic agent - prepare and handle using safe-handling precautions for hazardous drugs
Reconstitute and dilute per the product labelling; infuse IV over 30 minutes
Verify the calculated dose against body surface area; never exceed a single IV dose of 4 mg
Confirm baseline neutrophils >=1500/mm3 and platelets >=100,000/mm3 before the first cycle
Obtain blood counts before each cycle and frequently during therapy; apply dose modifications for toxicity
Manage extravasation and infusion reactions per institutional cytotoxic protocols
moa: Topotecan inhibits topoisomerase I, an enzyme that relieves torsional strain in DNA by inducing reversible single-strand breaks. Topotecan binds to and stabilises the topoisomerase I-DNA cleavable complex, preventing religation of these single-strand breaks. As the replication fork advances during the S phase of the cell cycle, it collides with the stabilised cleavable complexes, producing lethal double-strand DNA breaks. Mammalian cells cannot efficiently repair these double-strand breaks, leading to cell death. The cytotoxicity is therefore S-phase specific.

absolute: History of severe hypersensitivity reactions (including anaphylactoid reactions) to topotecan
Severe pre-existing bone marrow suppression (baseline neutrophils <1500/mm3 or platelets <100,000/mm3 for the first cycle)
relative: Pre-existing diarrhoea or risk of neutropenic enterocolitis
Concurrent radiotherapy or other myelosuppressive chemotherapy
monitor: Complete blood counts with differential and platelets

preg: Based on its mechanism and animal data, topotecan can cause fetal harm when administered to a pregnant woman; it is embryotoxic, fetotoxic and teratogenic. It should be avoided in pregnancy. Females of reproductive potential should use effective contraception during treatment and for a period after the last dose, and males with female partners of reproductive potential should also use contraception, as recommended in the labelling.
lact: It is not known whether topotecan is excreted in human milk, but because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in a breastfed infant, women should not breastfeed during treatment with topotecan and for several days after the final dose, per the labelling.
renal: Topotecan and its active metabolite are eliminated substantially by the kidneys. No adjustment is needed for mild renal impairment (CLcr 40-60 mL/min). For moderate impairment (CLcr 20-39 mL/min), reduce the dose (e.g. to 0.75 mg/m2/day). There are insufficient data to recommend a dose for severe impairment (CLcr <20 mL/min); use is not recommended.
hepatic: No dosage adjustment is recommended for patients with mild to moderate hepatic impairment (plasma bilirubin between 1.5 and 10 mg/dL). Topotecan is metabolised only to a minor extent by the liver.

major: Other myelosuppressive chemotherapy (additive haematologic toxicity - may require dose reduction)
Concurrent or sequential radiation therapy (increased myelosuppression and mucositis)
moderate: P-glycoprotein and BCRP inhibitors (e.g. ciclosporin, elacridar) can increase topotecan exposure
Cisplatin (used in combination for cervical cancer - greater myelosuppression)
minor: Live vaccines should be avoided during immunosuppressive chemotherapy
interactions.alcohol: No specific pharmacologic interaction; alcohol may worsen nausea and mucositis
interactions.diagnostics: Expect cytopenias on CBC; monitor liver enzymes which may rise

serious: Severe myelosuppression with febrile neutropenia and sepsis (BOXED WARNING)
emergency: Acute interstitial lung disease / respiratory failure

monitoring: Complete blood count with differential and platelet count before each cycle and frequently during treatment
Baseline neutrophils >=1500/mm3 and platelets >=100,000/mm3 before the first cycle
Renal function (dose depends on creatinine clearance)
Respiratory symptoms (cough, dyspnoea, fever) for interstitial lung disease
counsel: This is a chemotherapy medicine given as an infusion; you will have regular blood tests to check your blood counts
Report any fever, chills, sore throat, or signs of infection immediately - your white cells may be low
Report unusual bruising, bleeding, black stools, or nosebleeds (low platelets)
Tell your team about new cough, breathlessness, or fever (possible lung inflammation)
Severe or persistent diarrhoea, abdominal pain, or vomiting should be reported promptly
Hair loss can occur and is usually reversible
Use effective contraception during and after treatment; do not breastfeed; tell your doctor if you may be pregnant
pk: Cytotoxic effect develops over the 5-day cycle; antitumour response assessed over cycles
Peak plasma concentration at end of the 30-minute IV infusion
Given daily for 5 days each 21-day cycle; nadir of blood counts typically days 8-11
Store vials per labelling (typically 20-25 degrees C, protect from light); use reconstituted solution promptly
pearls: BOXED WARNING - severe myelosuppression is the dose-limiting toxicity; do NOT give the first cycle unless baseline neutrophils >=1500/mm3 and platelets >=100,000/mm3.
Dose strictly by body surface area and never exceed a single IV dose of 4 mg.
Reduce dose to 1.25 mg/m2 (or use G-CSF) after severe neutropenia; reduce for CLcr 20-39 mL/min and avoid if CLcr <20 mL/min.
Watch for neutropenic enterocolitis and interstitial lung disease - both can be fatal.
No hepatic dose adjustment needed for mild-moderate impairment; topotecan is mainly renally cleared.
Topotecan is teratogenic - mandatory effective contraception and no breastfeeding.
missed: Topotecan is administered by healthcare professionals on a fixed cycle schedule, so patients do not self-dose. If an infusion or appointment is missed, contact the oncology team to reschedule; do not attempt to make up doses, and the cycle timing will be adjusted by the prescriber based on blood counts and recovery.
overdose: Overdoses (up to 10-fold the recommended dose) have occurred with IV topotecan. The primary complication is severe myelosuppression. Elevated hepatic enzymes, mucositis, gastrointestinal toxicity, and skin toxicity have also occurred. There is no specific antidote. If overdose is suspected, monitor closely for myelosuppression and institute supportive care (haematologic support including transfusions and G-CSF, management of infection and mucositis) as appropriate.
